rv.q: As dramaturg, Oberman reverses six other characters, with Essendine’s secretary morphing from Monica to Monty, and the ex-spouse being Len not Liz. These re-gendered characters also have a new calendar and atlas, moving from mid 20th century London to New York in the 1970s (Studio 54 has just opened).

When Johannes, here gender-flipped and played by Kit Young , brusquely instructs her to sit down, it lands less as flirtation than control. Oberman is tremendous in the central role. She possesses the larger-than-life quality the part requires, moving effortlessly between diva-ish theatricality and flashes of genuine loneliness.
